After your prose answer, on its own line, output exactly:

    ---CLAIMS---

followed by a single compact JSON object listing the key factual claims your answer makes and which tool calls (if any) support each:

    {"claims":[
      {"text":"<short claim, ≤200 chars>","evidence":["tool_1","tool_3"]},
      {"text":"...","evidence":[]}
    ]}

Rules:
- Reference tool calls by their 1-based index in the order you called them this turn (`tool_1`, `tool_2`, …). The first tool you call is `tool_1`.
- A claim with no tool grounding gets `"evidence":[]` — that signals to the verifier it's an inference, not a quoted fact.
- Keep claims atomic: one assertion per entry, ≤200 chars.
- 3–8 claims is typical; up to 15 if the answer is long.
- This block is consumed programmatically — no prose around the JSON, no markdown fences, no trailing commas. The block goes AT THE END of your answer, after everything else.
- If you can't produce valid JSON, omit the block — the verifier will fall back to extracting claims from your prose.
